In a letter dated Tuesday and released on Wednesday, the 13 Democratic and Republican U.S. lawmakers said they 'strongly encourage' FIFA to move the global competition.

The simple hatchback is 50 years old this year. It may not be as fast as a Ferrari or as regal as a Rolls Royce, but it is the most popular car in the world. Originally designed to help French farmers move their sheep, the car now makes up two out of every three cars sold in the UK. It is popular worldwide, from Munich to Mexico City, because of its practical design, economy and comfort. The Renault 16, unveiled in April 1965, is credited as the world's first ever hatchback. The Renault 4 was the forerunner designed to allow French farmers to transport sheep.

Almeria have appointed Sergi Barjuan as their third coach this season. The 43-year-old replaces Juan Ignacio Martinez, who was fired after a 4-1 home defeat to Levante. Barjuan, a former Barcelona defender, will take the team to Barcelona on Wednesday, provided paperwork is complete. He made 53 Spain caps between 1998 and 2004, and played in two World Cups for La Roja. He coached Recreativo in Spain's second division from 2012-14.

From kittens for sale to handymen for hire, most newsagent ads are practical. But for one lonely heart, it was the perfect alternative to internet dating. A man known only as John used it to advertise for someone special. In the post, which has gone viral after being photographed and put online, he sets out his requirements and offers "a way of life with quality." John, who is reportedly a builder, posted this advert in his local newsagents. It has since gone viral after a passerby spotted it. John posted his advert, written in capital letters in black pen, in the window of his local newsagents in Muswell Hill.

Helsinborg manager Henrik Larsson was forced to play his 42-year-old Daniel Andersson in goal on Saturday. The former Celtic and Barcelona striker had no option but to play because goalkeepers Par Hansson and Matt Pyzdrowski were out injured. Astonishingly, the emergency stopper kept a clean sheet as Helsinborg drew 0-0 against Kalmar in the Allsvenskan season opener.

Spearing to local TV after the game, Andersson - a retired goalkeeper who earned one cap for Sweden in 2001 - said: 'It was a scenario that I never could have prepared myself for. Going from kit man, to goalie coach, to playing.'
